lines: A group class now holds one live link to the ride hub, and only while you ride it.
Join a group session and the app opens one connection to the hub, signed in with your session.
It asks the hub for its time five times and keeps the quickest answer, so every rider's clock agrees.
If the link drops, it tries again at once, then after two, five and ten seconds, then every thirty, and checks the clock again.
Ride alone, or just browse, and there is no connection at all.
The ride looks the same on every screen, with the link held quietly underneath.
What the tests prove: one connection, a measured clock, a quick return, and nothing left open.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
